name: Agent-protocol deep runner
description: An opt-in alternative worker that holds a two-way session with an agent over the Agent Client Protocol, so a message can be injected into the turn that is running through a steering poll or a direct call. It never raises and turns a missing package, old runtime or wedged turn into a clear unmet result.
advantages: Mid-run steering, so late user input need not wait for the next attempt, with typed protocol instead of parsed command-line output.
disadvantages: Extra dependencies and a recent Node runtime are needed, there is more to configure, and it buys nothing when no one steers.

name: Persistent stream-json runner
description: Holds one live Claude Code session per run over its stream-json input and output, so the person can steer, stop or pause while it works. A message is claimed only at the moment it is written to the session, so it arrives once and only for its own run; the model's replay of it marks it seen. A stop sends an interrupt and keeps the session, and a worker that ignores it is terminated and then killed after a grace period. A pause releases the process and resumes later on the same session. It keeps the live progress stream, resume, the subscription login, the usage-limit wait and the liveness review, and hands the run to the one-shot runner when the installed Claude Code cannot report an interrupt.
advantages: A message reaches the worker's next step within seconds instead of after the whole run, a stop takes effect at once and keeps finished work, a pause costs no memory while it waits, and a message that was written but not confirmed seen is handed back instead of being lost.
disadvantages: Not measured against live runs yet, so it is selected by nobody. It needs a Claude Code recent enough to answer an interrupt, a long-lived process per active run on a shared host, and its replay of a message is matched by text. The priority flag that should move work to the background did not do so in the probe, so only the default priority is used.

name: Hub's own tool loop
description: Works a goal with the hub's own loop instead of an external coding agent: a pure completion replies with actions (read, edit, run, check, delegate, report) that hub code runs in a sandbox, starting from a folder map with the relevant files already in view. This is the hub's runner with this runner's settings, handed the lane's own operations (raising a decision, adding a note to a goal) as tools that run in process, and giving its commands the same environment as the Claude Code worker; a decision raised through a tool is the run's decision id.
advantages: On the hub's cases it matched Claude Code's pass rate on the same model at a fraction of the cost (measured 2026-11-09), because calls are few and small and a passing self-check ends the run with no further call.
disadvantages: On trial: never chosen automatically, a lane runs it only when its configuration names it. Not yet run on this runner's own deep work; the worker has no skills or connected servers of its own, only shell commands in a sandbox, and web search and page reading through the lane's search backend, or through the Claude Code login when there is none (one agent process per search, so slower, and subject to the login's usage limits; WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED=false turns it off).

name: Hub's frame on the model's own tool loop
description: Works a goal in one lean Claude Code session on its own trained tools, prepared by the hub (the files that matter in view, an outline of the folder, what is left out and why, a short plan, discover before asking, this lane's skills folder named) and checked by the hub's code check of written text after it reports; stop, steer and resume are the stream runner's. This is the hub's runner with this runner's settings, named native_loop.
advantages: The model works in the format it is trained on and its own habits of looking things up (file history, a database file, the web, a command's output) apply, which the hub's text-protocol loop does not give it on long tool-heavy work; the hub's strengths (files already in view, the code check) are kept.
disadvantages: On trial: never chosen automatically, a lane runs it only when its configuration names it. Not yet run on this runner's own deep work. It has no in-process lane tools (create_decision, add_quest_note run through the command line in Bash, not behind the run's requester), loads no skills of its own so the frame names the skills folder, uses Claude Code's web tools and not the lane's search backend, carries the CLI's own system prompt on every run (dearer than hub_loop on tasks that end in one or two calls) and has no command sandbox of its own.
